subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.create` fail closed for every existing ownerless parent or target session, without a migration or operator recovery path in this PR?
rationale: Exact equality is the safer isolation boundary, but it intentionally removes access to persisted legacy ownerless rows and therefore needs explicit ownership and upgrade-policy approval.

options.title: Accept fail-closed legacy behavior
options.body: Land the exact-owner rule after real Gateway proof, treating ownerless persisted rows as unavailable to plugin-runtime creation flows.

options.title: Add an ownership migration
options.body: Define and test a doctor or operator-owned migration that assigns safe ownership before plugin runtimes can reuse legacy rows.

options.title: Coordinate all session RPCs
options.body: Pause this PR and the adjacent patch work until create, patch, delete, and reset share one owner-approved authorization contract.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed legacy behavior
recommendation.body: Land the exact-owner rule after real Gateway proof, treating ownerless persisted rows as unavailable to plugin-runtime creation flows.

likelyOwner.reason: Merged history most directly connects this person to the parent-link and dashboard session APIs whose security and upgrade semantics change here.
